back: A book of the New Testament that tells the good news about Jesus: Matthew, Mark, Luke or John.
Both mean "anointed one": Messiah is Hebrew and Christ is Greek. Christians believe Jesus is the Messiah.

front: Name the four Jewish groups in the time of Jesus.
Where was Jesus born and where did he grow up?
back: Born in Bethlehem; grew up in Nazareth, in Galilee.

front: Where is the baptism of Jesus told?
back: Mark 1:9-11 (also in Matthew, Luke and John). John the Baptist baptised him in the Jordan.

front: How many disciples did Jesus choose, and name two.
back: Twelve; for example Peter (Simon) and Andrew, James and John.

front: What happened at the Last Supper?
back: Jesus shared bread and wine with his disciples and spoke of his body and a new covenant.

front: Which Roman governor ordered the crucifixion?
Why is the resurrection central to Christianity?
back: Christians believe it shows that death is not the end and that Jesus is the Son of God; it is celebrated at Easter and on every Sunday.
